doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Starting the college concerts
summary: Iola explains how Mills College and Berkeley concerts led her to write to colleges, and Associated Booking made it a circuit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well let me rewind just a little bit again. What gave you the idea that jazz concerts, and Dave in particular, might do well in a college setting?

Oh about the college you mean? That was early. And that came about because when he was studying with Milhaud at Mills College, the musicians there all were full of great ideas and performed a concert that was fundraising for scholarships or something, and it was very enthusiastically received by the college population, especially among the music students. So then it seemed the idea was well we’ll do the same thing at UC Berkeley. So that was set up. And it became more and more apparent that commercially these same musicians were scrambling, trying to find jobs and playing odd places and doing commercial stuff that they didn’t want to do, and the general public not that interested. It was background music in a Chinese restaurant or something. But where the people were really interested and really listening were in the colleges. And so that’s when I had the idea, okay, I’ll find out the colleges up and down within driving distance of San Francisco, up and down the coast, and write to — usually to the student body — usually there is an arts division where they bring in entertainment. And so we sent out a lot of letters and got a few responses, but it just snowballed from there. And also right in the Bay area Dave had decided early on that the group would play for nothing or next to nothing at any school assembly, any situation where you were meeting young people. And so I think that was the beginning. And then after he had signed with Associated Booking, they took up the idea and they started contacting all of the colleges and first thing you know that became part of a circuit for everybody.
It’s almost a period piece in itself with the LPs “Jazz Goes to College.” Because now jazz lives in college.
